facts.fact: The Rope-Hut has a sprig of juniper nailed above its door and a door facing downhill; it lies about an hour's descent by cairn-light from the crew ledge on the south slope.
facts.why: needed to link the crew ledge of chapter 7 to the Rope-Hut

facts.fact: Asha's four, after losing the tracks on the bare ridge, cast east along the Saddle's lip rather than finding the ledge.
facts.why: needed to explain how Meera and Rohan escape them before the Rope-Hut

facts.fact: Meera hauls Rohan out of the gully with a sliding-grip two-to-one drag on the red rope anchored to her axe, which Bindu calls the lazy woman's lift.
facts.why: the beat requires a crew pulley trick

facts.fact: The crown redbark wrappers carry a faint round sieve-mark pressed into the wax along the fold, from the lowland guild stores' silk sieve with a ring in the weave.
facts.why: clue C07: Rohan identifies the redbark as crown-grade

facts.fact: The regent's hunters announce themselves with a two-note falling horn call that Meera recognises, and they climb the Neshar-side road with torches in a long line of fourteen or more.
facts.why: needed to identify the torches at the chapter's end
